outcomes: Record source and license provenance for every document
Apply explicit cleaning and inspect removed content
Detect exact and near duplicates with a documented similarity rule
Assign whole documents to stable splits and audit contamination
lessons: Split complete documents and test contamination

provenance.name: data provenance
provenance.definition: A record of where data came from, what terms govern it, and which transformations produced the training artifact.
provenance.explanation: Useful provenance connects each retained document to a source, author or publisher when known, license or terms, retrieval context, identity, and processing recipe. It supports reproducibility, rights review, debugging, and removal requests. A URL or mirror license does not establish rights to the text itself. Provenance records evidence rather than guaranteeing legality or quality. Model checkpoints should refer to the exact corpus manifest and tokenizer so later results can be traced to their inputs.

near-duplicate.name: near duplicate
near-duplicate.definition: A document substantially overlapping another after small formatting or content changes.
near-duplicate.explanation: Exact hashes miss copies that add navigation, alter whitespace, or edit a few words. Near-duplicate detectors compare features such as token shingles and remove pairs above a recorded threshold. The choice balances repeated-content leakage against false removal of legitimately related documents. Deduplication order also decides which copy survives. At scale, approximate search reduces cost, while an exact small implementation can remain an oracle. Removed-to-retained links make the decision auditable.

contamination.name: evaluation contamination
contamination.definition: Training exposure to evaluation items, answers, or close variants that weakens the meaning of held-out scores.
contamination.explanation: Contamination can arise through exact document copies, quoted benchmark questions, solution pages, neighboring windows, or semantically close variants. Document splitting and cross-split deduplication prevent common forms, while substring or paragraph checks catch items embedded in larger pages. Every detector has false negatives and false positives, so a clean report is evidence under a stated method rather than proof of absence. Evaluation data should remain untouched while training choices are made.

sources.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

checks: Malformed or empty documents return errors
Near-duplicate fixture removes the intended copy
Manifest retains source and license fields
Document IDs are unique and assigned to exactly one split
limitations: Quadratic pair comparison is for small corpora
FNV identity is not cryptographic authentication
The fixture does not demonstrate language or PII filtering
